plan.summary: This 1-4 block is an off-camp rebuild with an endurance bias for boxing while still keeping a small dose of power, strength, trunk, and neck work. Week 1 establishes simple bodyweight baselines so later blocks can progress from something real. Weeks 2-3 build repeatable work capacity and boxing-specific conditioning, and Week 4 deloads volume to freshen up before the next block review.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Establish basic bodyweight strength baselines and build aerobic and repeated-effort conditioning without excessive soreness.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress conditioning density and repeatable effort while keeping enough strength and power work to support boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep conditioning specific and sharp with lower fatigue while preserving the strength and power you built.

exercises.name: 1a. Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Reset between reps. Land softly and keep every jump crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the squat jump feels awkward. Same focus on fast takeoff and soft landing.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low safe box if space allows. Step down each rep.

exercises.name: 1b. Plyo Push-Up
exercises.notes: Explode off the floor but keep the body straight. Use hands-elevated if full floor reps are not clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Plyo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Safer beginner option if you cannot leave the floor cleanly.

substitutionOptions.name: Fast Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Move up as fast as possible if impact on the wrists is not ideal.

exercises.name: 2. Push-Up Baseline Test
exercises.notes: One all-out clean set to establish your current baseline. Stop when form breaks, not after ugly reps.

performanceTarget.prompt: Log your best clean set so the next block can progress from a real baseline.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up Baseline Test
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor push-ups are not yet consistent. Record the surface height used.

exercises.name: 3. Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use full control and stay tall. Front foot flat, back knee travels down smoothly.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Good option if split squat balance is limiting the set.

substitutionOptions.name: Bodyweight Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if split squats are too unstable right now.

exercises.name: 4. Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Use a table, bar, or rings if available. Pull the chest up and keep the body rigid. Stop with 1-2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a sturdy setup only. Keep tension even and move under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Pull hard against a fixed anchor for 15-20 seconds if no row setup is available.

exercises.name: 5. Forearm Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, ribs down, glutes tight. Do not let the low back sag.

substitutionOptions.name: High Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if forearm position is uncomfortable.

substitutionOptions.name: Hollow Body Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a harder trunk option and can keep the low back flat.

exercises.name: 6. Supine Neck Isometric Series
exercises.notes: Light pressure only. Do front, back, left, and right holds with smooth breathing and no pain.

substitutionOptions.name: Standing Hand-Resisted Neck Isometrics
substitutionOptions.notes: Use gentle hand pressure and keep the neck long.

exercises.name: 7. Shadow Boxing Tempo Intervals
exercises.notes: Smooth technical pace. Build rhythm and breathing, not a sprint.

endurancePrescription.target: Boxing-specific aerobic base and movement rhythm
endurancePrescription.notes: Stay relaxed. Keep footwork, guard recovery, and clean mechanics.

exercises.name: 6. Boxing Conditioning Circuit

endurancePrescription.target: Whole-body work capacity with boxing-specific fatigue resistance
endurancePrescription.notes: Move continuously but do not rush. Keep each station clean and repeatable.

circuitPrescription.targetAreaEmphasis: About 60% general work capacity and 40% boxing-specific fatigue resistance
circuitPrescription.progression: Add one round or add 5 seconds of work per station next block if quality stays high.
circuitPrescription.analytics: Track whether output and technique stay even from first round to last round.

substitutionOptions.name: Shadow Boxing Conditioning Circuit
substitutionOptions.notes: Use rounds of stance movement, straight punches, squat thrusts, and mountain climbers if space is tight.
